title: Current-mirror OTA
description: A current-mirror (or current-amplifier) OTA: the input pair drives diode-connected PMOS mirror loads, and each mirror is copied with ratio $K_m$ to an output branch — one side straight to the output, the other down through a bottom NMOS mirror — so the effective output transconductance is $K_m*g_{m,in}$ to first order. This buys bandwidth and slew almost for free — GBW = $K_m*g_{m,in}/(2*\pi*C_L)$ and SR = $K_m*I_{tail}/C_L$, to the same order — but not DC gain: raising $K_m$ scales both the output transconductance and the output conductance together, so the low-frequency gain is nearly independent of $K_m$. The mirrors are stated the way the circuit has them: each output device sits on its diode device's gate at a multiple of that device's width, and its current is read from the table at its own drain voltage. Nothing is trimmed to make a copy exact, so the ratios the rows report are $K_m$ moved by each mirror's drain-voltage error, the two output devices do not ask for the same current, and the systematic-offset row reports what that costs. One current is typed — half the tail current, into the PMOS diode device — and every other device reads another device's current or takes it through a shared gate. One node is solved besides the tail node: the NMOS diode's, which sits at that diode's own gate-source voltage at the current the PMOS output device above it delivers there. The catch of the topology shows up in noise: to hit a fixed GBW at larger $K_m$ the input pair shrinks ($g_{m,in}$ falls as $1/K_m$), so its input-referred thermal density grows as $\sqrt{K_m}$. Two mirror nodes carry poles: the PMOS node every branch passes (a full pole), and the bottom NMOS node only the folded branch passes (a pole-zero doublet). Both estimates are shown; settling is sim-owned.

params.name: vn_target
params.note: input-referred thermal density budget. the budget carries about 30% headroom over the gamma-model row (no measured floor exists for this topology)

params.name: V_out_dc
params.note: output DC level; sets the vds of the two mirror output devices that meet at the output. They push and pull against each other at a high-impedance output that nothing on this sheet holds; the feedback the application closes around the amplifier holds it here. The two do not ask for the same current at this level, and the systematic-offset row reports what that costs

params.name: CM_lo
params.note: input CM range the application presents, low edge — checked exactly by the cm-lo edge at every evaluation (the sweep put the widest closing range at 0.89-1.42 V on sky130 tt at the shipped choices). The edge checks the ENDPOINT; the interior is the sweep's to show

params.name: CM_hi
params.note: input CM range the application presents, high edge — its ENDPOINT checked by the cm-hi edge the same way

params.name: CM_dc
params.note: the input common mode the application presents. The engine places the tail node so the sheet sits exactly here; sweep it to trace the common-mode axis

params.name: V_tail
params.note: the tail node — the pair's source. Solved rather than set: bisected between min and max (the BRACKET) until the produced common mode equals CM_dc. Fixes the pair's body bias and drain-source voltage in one stroke. The max must stay below the diode-loaded drain (VDD minus the mirror's |vgs|) — both bracket ends have to size

params.name: V_nmir
params.note: the NMOS diode's node — the gate and drain of the bottom mirror's diode device, and the drain of the PMOS output device that feeds it. Solved, not set: that PMOS device's drain-source voltage is what is left between the supply and this node, the current it delivers there is the current the diode carries, and the diode's own gate-source voltage at that current is this node. The engine iterates until the two agree, so the stored value is only the starting guess. Where the diode is sized for its inversion level its gate-source voltage does not depend on the current and the first substitution lands; with the diode held at its width — at a range end or at another process condition — it does

params.name: sign_p
params.note: vds sign convention of the PMOS-side tables: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis. Only the two PMOS output devices read it — the diode device's drain follows its own gate in whichever convention its table uses. Read all three PMOS devices from the same table: the gate voltage they share is passed in that table's convention

params.name: I_tail
params.note: the tail current the bias network programs. No tail device is on this sheet, so its half is typed into exactly one device, the PMOS diode device, and the input device in the same branch reads that device's current. Every mirror output device takes its current through the gate it shares, so transconductance, slew rate and supply current are computed from what the devices deliver, not from this number

params.name: K_m
params.note: mirror ratio, as a width ratio: each PMOS output device is K_m times its diode device's width on the same gate. Multiplies GBW and SR, but raises input noise as sqrt(K_m) at fixed GBW. The current ratio a mirror delivers differs from K_m by that mirror's drain-voltage error

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets gm per current and the input-referred noise floor

params.name: gm_id_ml
params.note: mirror inversion, set on the two diode devices (the PMOS one and the bottom NMOS one) and inherited by each output device through the gate it shares: sets the mirror-node poles, and lower gm/ID gives the output devices a higher output resistance

params.name: L_mir
params.note: length of every mirror device — a diode device and the output devices on its gate mirror at one length: longer shrinks each mirror's drain-voltage error and raises the output resistance

doc.title: Input mirror device (diode)
doc.description: Diode-connected mirror load carrying half the tail current — the one device on this sheet whose current is typed. Its drain is its gate, so its $V_{DS}$ is its own $V_{GS}$ and the table is read along that diagonal with nothing estimated; its gate node carries the mirror pole. The circuit has one of these on each side of the pair, identical at balance, so this block stands for both. It publishes its width and its gate voltage, which is all a PMOS output device needs to copy it, and its current, which the input device in the same branch reads.

doc.title: Input-pair device
doc.description: Half-circuit input device, in one branch with the diode mirror load above it and carrying that device's current. Its source sits at the tail node — that is its body bias — and its drain one diode drop below the supply, so its drain-source voltage is what is left between the two.

doc.title: Output mirror device (PMOS side)
doc.description: The PMOS mirror's output device at the output node: $K_m$ times the diode device's width on the diode device's gate. Its current is read off the table rather than typed — the diode device sits at its own gate-source voltage and this device at $V_{DD} - V_{out,dc}$, so it delivers $K_m$ times the diode's current scaled by what that difference in $V_{DS}$ does through its $g_{ds}$. Its gds is one half of the output conductance and its gate cap loads the mirror node.

params.name: W_o
params.note: K_m times the diode device's width

params.name: vgs_o
params.note: the diode device's gate voltage — the mirror node the two share, in the sign convention of the diode device's table

params.name: vds_o
params.note: the supply down to the output, signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Output mirror device (PMOS side, feeding the bottom mirror)
doc.description: The other PMOS mirror's output device: the same $K_m$-wide copy on the diode device's gate, with its drain on the NMOS diode's node instead of at the output. It sits at $V_{DD} - V_{nmir}$, not at the output's drain voltage, so it delivers a different current from the device at the output, and that current is what the bottom mirror is handed. Its drain voltage and the current it delivers there set each other through the NMOS diode below it, which is the one loop this sheet closes.

params.name: W_o
params.note: K_m times the diode device's width

params.name: vgs_o
params.note: the diode device's gate voltage — the mirror node the two share, in the sign convention of the diode device's table

params.name: vds_o
params.note: the supply down to the NMOS diode's node, signed to this table's axis convention

doc.title: Bottom mirror device (NMOS diode)
doc.description: The diode-connected NMOS that folds the second branch down to the bottom output device: one input branch reaches the output through its PMOS mirror alone, the other continues through this device to moutn. It carries the current the PMOS output device above it delivers, read from that device rather than typed; its gate node is the second mirror pole. Diode-connected, so its drop is read off the vds = vgs diagonal — and that drop is the node the PMOS device above it has its drain on. It publishes its width and its gate voltage for the bottom output device to copy.

doc.title: Output mirror device (NMOS side)
doc.description: The bottom mirror's output device: the NMOS diode device's width on the NMOS diode device's gate, a 1:1 copy with its drain at the output. Its current is read off the table at $V_{out,dc}$ rather than typed. It is a copy of a copy, so it carries the drain-voltage error of both mirrors in its path, and what it sinks differs from what the PMOS device at the output sources. Its gds is the other half of the output conductance.

params.name: W_o
params.note: the NMOS diode device's width — a 1:1 copy

params.name: vgs_o
params.note: the NMOS diode device's gate voltage — the mirror node the two share

params.name: vds_o
params.note: the output level

equations.name: CM_in
equations.note: the input common mode this bias produces — an OUTPUT here, not a setting; rises monotonically with the tail node, so the pin is a well-posed bisection

equations.name: Ai_p
equations.note: small-signal current gain of the PMOS mirror that drives the output directly: the output device's gm over its diode device's. It is the width ratio K_m moved by the difference between the two drain voltages

equations.name: Ai_n
equations.note: small-signal current gain of the path through the bottom mirror: the other PMOS mirror's gain times the NMOS mirror's. Two copies in series, so it carries two drain-voltage errors

equations.name: Gm_out
equations.note: output transconductance: each input device turns half the differential input into current, and each half reaches the output through its own mirror path. It is K_m times the input gm where both paths copy exactly

equations.name: Rout
equations.note: output node loaded by the conductance of both output devices, each read where its mirror puts it: on its diode device's gate, at the output's drain voltage. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

equations.name: Av
equations.note: DC gain; K_m scales Gm_out and (via the K_m-wider output devices) Rout inversely, so gain is nearly K_m-independent

equations.name: GBW
equations.note: dominant-pole gain-bandwidth into the load, from the transconductance the two mirror paths deliver

equations.name: SR
equations.note: the whole tail current steered to one side of the pair is twice what that side carries at rest, so the output device at the end of that side's mirror path delivers twice its quiescent current to first order. Rising, that is the PMOS output device; falling, the NMOS one. The two differ by the mirrors' drain-voltage errors, and this is the slower direction

equations.name: vn_in
equations.note: input pair plus the mirror load's own density referred by gm_mload/gm_in

equations.name: vn_gbw
equations.note: estimate: input density if the pair were sized to just meet GBW_target at this K_m — grows as sqrt(K_m), the current-mirror OTA's noise-for-bandwidth trade

equations.name: f_pole
equations.note: estimate: the PMOS mirror-node pole, set by the diode device's gm over its own gate cap plus that of the K_m-times-wider output device on the same node. Read on the side that drives the output; the other side's node carries a device of the same width at a different drain voltage

equations.name: f_pole_n
equations.note: estimate: the bottom NMOS mirror-node pole, same accounting as f_pole on the folded branch: the diode device's gm, at the current it is handed, over its own gate cap plus that of the equal-width output device

equations.name: PM
equations.note: estimate: the two mirror nodes cost phase differently, because the signal reaches them differently. BOTH input branches pass a PMOS mirror node, so $f_{pole}$ is a full pole in the whole path — unlike the 5T's mirror. Only the folded branch passes the bottom NMOS mirror, so half the signal is delayed there and $f_{pole,n}$ is a pole-ZERO DOUBLET (zero at twice the pole), costing far less phase. Measured against the ACHIEVED GBW, so overshooting the bandwidth target spends margin honestly

equations.name: vos_sys
equations.note: estimate: input-referred systematic offset. The output node takes the PMOS output device's current in and the NMOS output device's current out. Each is a copy made at a drain voltage that is not its diode device's, and the NMOS one is a copy of a copy, so the two do not ask for the same current at $V_{out,dc}$. With $V_{out,dc}$ held by a loop outside this sheet, that difference has to come from an input imbalance of this size. Reported only; no check reads it

equations.name: cgg_in
equations.note: estimate: the capacitance one input terminal presents — the gate capacitance of a single input device. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

equations.name: I_q
equations.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the two input branches, each through its PMOS diode device, plus the branches of the two PMOS output devices, each at the current that device delivers at its own drain voltage. The bottom mirror adds nothing: it carries to ground current already counted on the PMOS side. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no check reads it

checks.note: computed from the gamma-model floor; this table carries no measured noise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
estimate: margin left at crossover once the mirror node is paid for; advisory, since an open-loop OTA needs none of it and sim owns the real stability
trips when the tail node is pushed so high the pair runs out of drain-source voltage under the diode load — lower gm/ID on the mirror spends less diode drop
the common mode this bias produces has to sit inside the range the application presents
paired with cm-not-below; the cm-lo/cm-hi edges check that the design covers the range ENDS, and the CM_dc sweep shows the whole landscape

operatingRange.name: cm-lo
operatingRange.note: the claimed low edge, checked exactly: the whole sheet re-evaluates at CM_dc = CM_lo on the design this run produced — its own tail-node solve from the full bracket, every device held at the geometry it was sized to — and every hard rule must hold there

operatingRange.name: cm-hi
operatingRange.note: the claimed high edge, checked the same way. The edges check the ENDPOINTS; the CM_dc sweep remains the authority on the full landscape
